question: When did Constantinople fall to the Ottoman Turks?
fact: Sultan Mehmed II took the city on 29 May 1453 after a siege of about seven weeks, using some of the largest cannons ever built.

question: When was the Treaty of Versailles signed?
fact: It was signed on 28 June 1919, five years to the day after Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot in Sarajevo.

question: When was US President John F. Kennedy assassinated?
fact: Kennedy was shot in Dallas, Texas, on 22 November 1963, while riding in an open car.

question: When did the Bolsheviks seize power in Russia's October Revolution?
fact: By the calendar Russia used then it was October 1917. By ours it was 7 November.

question: When was Nelson Mandela released from prison?
fact: Mandela walked free on 11 February 1990 after 27 years in prison, most of them on Robben Island.

question: When was Charlemagne crowned emperor by the Pope?
fact: Pope Leo III crowned Charlemagne in St Peter's in Rome on Christmas Day in the year 800.

question: When did the Spanish Armada sail against England?
fact: Storms off Scotland and Ireland wrecked more of the 1588 Armada than English guns did.

question: When did Britain's Parliament pass the Slavery Abolition Act?
fact: The act was passed in 1833 and came into force in 1834, ending slavery in most of the British Empire.

question: When did the Cuban Missile Crisis happen?
fact: For 13 days in October 1962 the US and the Soviet Union stood closer to nuclear war than at any other time.

question: When did New Zealand become the first country to give women the vote in national elections?
fact: Kate Sheppard's petition for the vote was signed by nearly 32,000 women, the biggest petition New Zealand had seen.

question: When did the first voyage around the world, Magellan's expedition, return to Spain?
fact: Only one ship, the Victoria, made it back in 1522, under Juan Sebastián Elcano. Magellan had been killed in the Philippines in 1521.

question: In what year BC was the Battle of Marathon fought?
fact: The Athenians beat a Persian army at Marathon in 490 BC. The legend of a runner carrying the news to Athens inspired the modern marathon.

question: In what year BC was Rome founded, according to legend?
fact: Legend says Romulus founded Rome on 21 April 753 BC, after killing his twin brother Remus.

question: When was the last Western Roman emperor, Romulus Augustulus, deposed?
fact: The Germanic general Odoacer deposed the teenage Romulus Augustulus in 476 and made himself King of Italy.

question: When did the Peace of Westphalia end the Thirty Years' War?
fact: The treaties were signed in the German cities of Osnabrück and Münster in 1648.

question: When was the Rosetta Stone found?
fact: French soldiers found it near Rashid (Rosetta) in Egypt in 1799. It carries the same decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek.

question: When did Howard Carter find Tutankhamun's tomb?
fact: Carter found the steps down to the tomb in November 1922, after years of digging in the Valley of the Kings.

question: When did the American Civil War begin?
fact: The war began in April 1861 when Confederate guns fired on Fort Sumter in Charleston, South Carolina.

question: When did India become independent from Britain?
fact: India became independent at midnight on 15 August 1947. Pakistan had become independent the day before.

question: When did Guy Fawkes and his fellow plotters try to blow up Parliament?
fact: Fawkes was caught under the House of Lords on the night of 4–5 November 1605, guarding 36 barrels of gunpowder.

question: When did the Mayflower carry the Pilgrims to America?
fact: The Mayflower left Plymouth, England, in September 1620 with about 100 passengers and reached Cape Cod in November.
